results.title: Gauth Review 2026: Is This AI Homework Helper Worth It? | AgentFinder
results.content:
Gauth is built for students who hit a wall on a specific problem and need an explanation fast, not for students looking for a structured course or curriculum. If your study pattern looks like "I'm stuck on problem 7, I need to understand why," Gauth's photo-to-solution flow and step-by-step explanations are exactly the right shape of tool.

Gauth fits particularly well for:

Gauth is a weaker fit for students who need sustained, structured learning over weeks, like exam prep built around spaced repetition or a full course curriculum. For that kind of long-horizon studying, a dedicated platform like Study Genius AI may serve better, since Gauth is architected around solving the problem in front of you rather than building a study plan around what you'll need to know next month. [...] The category Gauth competes in sits between pure AI chatbots and dedicated study platforms like Study Genius AI. Where a general chatbot requires you to type out a problem (which is often the hardest part with math notation or diagrams), Gauth's visual input removes that friction entirely. That's the core value proposition: speed from problem to explanation, with minimal setup.

Gauth's feature set centers on four capabilities: photo-to-solution solving, conversational follow-up, multi-agent assignment processing, and source-linked topic research through Atlas. Each targets a different point in a student's workflow, from a single tricky problem to an entire assignment to open-ended research. [...] Gauth earns a 7/10 for nailing the core use case: turning a photo of a stuck-on problem into a clear, explained solution in seconds. The photo-first input, step-by-step explanations, and Assignment Solver for longer files make Gauth genuinely useful for day-to-day homework friction. Where Gauth falls short is pricing transparency and depth for students who need structured, long-term study support rather than one-off problem solving. If your need is "I'm stuck on this specific problem right now," Gauth is a strong, fast choice. If you need a structured study plan across a whole semester, pair it with or consider a dedicated platform like Study Genius AI instead.

results.title: Gauth Alternatives Ranked by Price, Accuracy, and Subject - Nibble Blog
results.content:
## What Gauth offers, and where it falls short

Gauth's core strength is speed: point a camera at a problem, and within seconds there's a step-by-step solution instead of a blank page.

The app covers the following:

- Camera-based scanning that reads typed and handwritten text.
- Step-by-step solution display for most math and science problems.
- Multi-subject support that stretches into biology, chemistry, and general homework help.
- Optional live-tutor add-on for problems the AI can't crack alone.
- Mobile-first design built for on-the-go use.

Gauth can misread handwriting or multi-step word problems, and that's where most accuracy complaints start.

Some tutor-chat apps, including SmartyMe, pair AI with human backup in a similar way, though subject depth varies from app to app. [...] A few deserve a closer look. Wolfram Alpha works as an AI math solver that pairs well with graphing tools such as GeoGebra, and Mathway covers similar ground for algebra.

Khan Academy leans on full video lessons instead of quick textbook solutions, suited to rebuilding a subject from scratch. Socratic by Google sits at the other end, built for a fast multi-subject nudge.

ChatGPT or Gemini work more like an open-ended AI study tool, useful for follow-up questions through ongoing AI chat rather than a single scanned answer.

## How Gauth reads a photo and returns an answer

Gauth, formerly GauthMath, is an AI homework helper owned by ByteDance. Students snap a photo of a problem and get an AI-generated answer with step-by-step solutions. [...] There's also an option to chat with a human tutor if the AI gets stuck, though the app works more like a quick AI tutor than a full teaching tool.

Gauth started as a math app and later expanded into biology and chemistry, with some writing help too. The basic flow from scan to answer looks like this:

1. Snap a photo of the problem.
2. The AI scans and reads the text.
3. You get an instant answer with steps shown.
4. If needed, open a live chat with a human tutor.

The free tier covers a limited number of daily scans, and the paid plan unlocks unlimited scans plus faster responses.
